pr_title: py/builtinevex: Handle invalid filenames for execfile.
pr_body:
Fixes #12522.

If a non-string buffer was passed to execfile, then it would be passed as a non-null-terminated char* to mp_lexer_new_from_file.

This changes mp_lexer_new_from_file to take a qstr instead (as in almost all cases a qstr will be created from this input anyway).

This now makes execfile require a string (not generic buffer) argument, which is probably a good fix to make anyway.

_This work was funded through GitHub Sponsors._

issue_context.title: Null pointer dereference in mp_reader_new_file
issue_context.body:
# Description

We found a null-dereference in the UNIX port version. All PoCs involve `builtins.execfile()` and crash in `mp_reader_new_file` eventually. We've attached three PoCs and their stack trace from ASAN.

[poc.zip](https://github.com/micropython/micropython/files/12729197/poc.zip)


# Proof of Concept

```
$ # build unix port with ASAN, at the root source code directory.
$ export CC=clang
$ export CXX=clang++
$ export CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
$ export CXXFLAGS=$CFLAGS
$ export LDFLAGS=$CFLAGS
$ export DEBUG=1
$ make -C mpy-cross -j
$ make -C ports/unix -j all lib
$
$ # run a poc.
$ export ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0"
$ ./ports/unix/build-standard/micropython <poc_file>
```


# Environment

Ubuntu 20.04
Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 5218 CPU @ 2.30GHz
Memory: 64 GB


# Affected Version

v1.20.0 (commit a3862e726, latest as of 2023-09-26)
v1.20.0 (commit 813d559bc, 2023-06-19)


# Question

We actually found many more crashes with ASAN other than this (including buffer-overflow), but we'd need some advice from `micropython` maintainers before posting issues for all of them.

  1) Do you also consider ASAN crashes through the UNIX port version relevant?
  2) How do you prefer accepting buffer-overflow cases? (via e-mail or via here) We haven't verified their exploitability.

Please let me report the rest of the crashes following your advice. Thank you very much for maintaining `micropython`.
comments:
Thanks for the detailed report @gwangmu.

This particular issue should be fixed by https://github.com/micropython/micropython/pull/12526

> Do you also consider ASAN crashes through the UNIX port version relevant?

Definitely. Please continue to report them.

> How do you prefer accepting buffer-overflow cases? (via e-mail or via here) We haven't verified their exploitability.

I understand why you're asking, but given the fixes are going to be public anyway we don't really have the resources to do a bigger process (and I'm not sure what that would achieve). I'm happy to just repeat exactly what you've done here. @dpgeorge WDYT?

> I'm happy to just repeat exactly what you've done here

Yes that's fine, to just open an issue with each of them.  But if there are many, I suggest starting with just a few and we'll see how they go.
Thank you very much @jimmo @dpgeorge . We'll make sure to control the posting pace depending on how it develops.

review_comments: For the case where it's importing a .mpy file, this now interns the filename when it didn't before.

It always interns the filename as it sets the `__file__` attribute to the same value in `do_execute_raw_code`. This is true for all imports (.py, .mpy, frozen). I've updated the PR to make this more explicit (and save it having to search for the now-already-interned value).

Technically `__file__` might be disabled, but it is enabled at level=core.

You're right, `do_execute_raw_code` is interning the filename... it just seems a bit off to me that you now need to pass a qstr as a filename everywhere (for lexing, etc) instead of a const-char-*.  But I guess that's the way everything is structured, and the reason for that is so that tracebacks can include the filename easily.
Couldn't the fix simply be to use `mp_obj_str_get_str` here?

Yes but now you have two copies of the string. One made here, another made in `mp_reader_new_file`.

Also one day we might want to not make str and/or qstr null terminated, so I'm always hesitant to make this dependency worse.

Well, `mp_obj_str_get_str` doesn't create anything, it just returns a pointer to the already-null-terminated data.  So using that function would be a very simple fix for this problem, and not allocate any additional RAM.  Then the larger qstr change is an optimisation.
